ld.name: The PuLi Shanghai in Shanghai
ld.description: It’s the city of the future, Shanghai — lucky, then, that its hotels, as a class, have quickly joined the ranks of the best in the world. For a little evidence supporting that proposition one needs to look no further than The PuLi Shanghai. Where one might expect another outpost of the established big-luxury chains, we find the flagship of a new group, The PuLi Group — they’re saving the poetry, it seems, for the product itself.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Amanyangyun in Shanghai
ld.description: What do you do when you’ve got an undistinguished parcel of land just outside of Shanghai, and, 700 kilometers away, in Jianxi Province, a collection of historic homes, dating back to the Ming and Qing dynasties, that are about to be subsumed by a dam project? If you’re Mr. Ma Dadong, an entrepreneur and Jianxi native, you spare no expense in rescuing the homes, moving them — brick by brick, stone by stone — to the site of your luxury resort: Amanyangyun. And, just for good measure, you transport a complete forest as well, comprising more than ten thousand centuries-old camphor trees, to provide Amanyangyun with a suitably picturesque backdrop.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Amandayan in Lijiang
ld.description: By this point an Aman hotel hardly needs vetting, true, but it remains a pleasure to detail their ongoing success story. They’ve hit photogenic gold again here in Lijiang, jewel of China’s Yunnan province, an astoundingly well-preserved repository for the region’s heritage and peerless natural beauty. Amandayan overlooks the impossibly ancient Old Town, a rich lattice of irreplaceable artifacts and architecture with a whimsical penchant for bridges and cobblestone streets.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Capella Shanghai, Jian Ye Li in Shanghai
ld.description: Shanghai’s Xuhui district is notable for its 20th-century shikumen laneways, narrow roads lined with traditional brick townhouses. They’re a rarity in the high-rise era, but some have been preserved for their architectural heritage, and a few of them find new life as villas in the luxurious Capella Shanghai, Jian Ye Li. The three-story villas’ extravagant interiors incorporate both French and Chinese influences, courtesy of designer Jaya Ibrahim, as well as the full complement of modern comforts, from Bose sound systems to Frédéric Malle bath amenities.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

address.streetAddress: No. 2 Changjiang Binjiang Road, Yuzhong District

ld.name: InterContinental Chongqing Raffles City in Chongqing
ld.description: The super-highrise buildings that tower over Chongqing’s busy Yuzhong district are both architecturally striking and meaningfully positioned at the confluence of two rivers, once the site of the city’s old imperial gate. InterContinental Chongqing Raffles City occupies a unique space within the ultramodern complex: while rooms and suites are housed within one of the vertical towers, the hotel’s lobby and dining venues are located in the Crystal, a “horizontal skyscraper" elevated 75 stories above the street.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Rosewood Beijing in Beijing
ld.description: If you’re skeptical of a hotel that calls itself an “urban village,” try to reserve your judgment for just a moment. It’s true that the hoteliers behind the Rosewood Beijing get a bit high-concept at times — what we’d call a concierge, the hotel refers to as “Rosewood curators.” But look past the branding exercises and you’ll find an exceedingly professional, exceptionally well-executed hotel, and one that’s packed with local character.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

address.streetAddress: No. 32 The Bund, 32 Zhongshan, Dong Yi Road

ld.name: The Peninsula Shanghai in Shanghai
ld.description: If, as we contend, Shanghai is going to be the future’s unofficial capital, it’s going to need more extraordinary hotels of every description — not just modern-design boutique hotels but classic grand hotels as well. The Peninsula Shanghai, on that score, certainly qualifies as a rather large step in the right direction; with its soaring, marble-clad Art Deco lobby (and its location on the Bund, a location where classic architecture is the rule) it already feels like it’s been here more or less forever.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

rest: Lin Family of One - The Bund
h2: Lin Family of One - The Bund

address.streetAddress: No. 366 Shi Men Yi Road, Jing’an

ld.name: Upper House Shanghai in Shanghai
ld.description: If you’ve been to Upper House Hong Kong or the Upper House Chengdu, then all you need to know is that the Upper House Shanghai is the third member of the same Upper House group. For the rest of us — or, to pass the time before your flight to Shanghai boards — we’ll elaborate. Upper House Shanghai’s interiors are by no less a light than Piero Lissoni, the Milanese architect and designer whose furniture adorns a substantial proportion of our favorite hotels in Italy and beyond. And here, his focused, near-monochrome modernist style is applied to Shanghai’s own distinctive visual language, to astonishing effect.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

rest: Rongjia Noodles Soup with Yellow Croaker (Jingan)
Ding Te Le Zhou Mian Guan
h2: Rongjia Noodles Soup with Yellow Croaker (Jingan)
Ding Te Le Zhou Mian Guan

ld.name: Yangshuo Sugar House in Guilin
ld.description: China’s hospitality scene is a dramatic blend of the historical and the ultra-modern — sometimes within the same hotel. A memorable example is the Yangshuo Sugar House Hotel, where the Beijing-based Vector Architects have transformed a disused sugar mill — which just happens to be set in an extraordinarily dramatic riverside landscape — into an inspired piece of contemporary post-industrial architecture and expanding it into a fantastically inventive luxury resort.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: 2 Dong Ruan Da Dao, Qingcheng Mountain Town, Dujiangyan

ld.name: Six Senses Qing Cheng Mountain in Chengdu
ld.description: There are the ordinary five senses: hearing, sight, touch, smell, and taste. And then there’s the sixth sense. Perceiving the imperceptible is a tantalizingly mysterious concept: it’s no wonder that it’s inspired filmmakers, poets, musicians, and even hoteliers, like those behind the Six Senses hotels, resorts, and spas. Six Senses Qing Cheng Mountain is one of the brand’s newest offerings, and its first in China, strategically located outside Chengdu, near two cultural attractions that bring a steady stream of visitors to the region: the ancient Dujiangyan irrigation system, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in its own right, and Mount Qing Cheng, better known as the birthplace of Taoism.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Upper House Chengdu in Chengdu
ld.description: Joining the same Swire family that brought us the Upper House Hong Kong and the Upper House Shanghai, the Upper House Chengdu might feel a bit more of a stretch for Western visitors. But it won’t be for long. Already a manufacturing center for many high-tech industries, it’ll be a more frequent destination in the coming years for global techies of all stripes — and they’ll be happy to find at least one world-class hotel awaiting them upon arrival.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Kimpton Bamboo Grove Suzhou in Suzhou
ld.description: For Kimpton’s first hotel in mainland China, the brand chose an unusual location: not Shanghai proper, but Suzhou, an hour and change to the west. And rather than import the chain’s Californian look and approach wholesale, the Kimpton Suzhou Bamboo Grove meticulously tailors its experience to its setting. The result is a dynamic fusion of local architecture and planning, embodied here as a series of low buildings surrounded by gardens and canals, with ultra-swanky modern hospitality design.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: InterContinental Resort Jiuzhai Paradise in Jiuzhaigou
ld.description: Any question about whether the word “paradise” is warranted should be put to rest by a look at the Jiuzhaigou Valley; the mountainous backdrop for the InterContinental Resort Jiuzhai Paradise is nothing short of spectacular. This ultra-modern steel-and-glass structure is immersed in dense forest, and is set just a few minutes’ drive from the Jiuzhaigou Nature Reserve, which is, somehow, even more wild and picturesque.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: 66th Jinshamen Road, Jiangbei District, Jiang Bei

ld.name: Regent Chongqing in Chongqing
ld.description: The reborn Regent brand is aimed squarely at the high end of the luxury-hotel market, and their selection encompasses both rural resorts and urban business hotels — and the Regent Chongqing is a member of the latter category. Of course, at this end of the hospitality world, the distinction is more about location than about concept; while the busy port city of Chongqing is a more likely destination for business travel than for rest and relaxation, a stay at the Regent Chongqing will be as restorative as you allow it to be.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Capella Tufu Bay in Lingshui
ld.description: China is increasingly where you go to see the most impressive modern luxury hotels, and that’s certainly true of this one — Capella Tufu Bay is a collaboration between architects Jean-Michel Gathy and Bill Bensley, both hospitality design all-stars. The public spaces are monumental, especially the circular lobby with its ornamental pool, and the rooms and villas are suitably residential — at their substantial size you wouldn’t call them “cozy,” but they’re warm and plush even as they verge on opulence.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: InterContinental Quanzhou in Quanzhou
ld.description: The InterContinental brand encompasses everything from lavish mountain resorts to equally lavish skyscraper-bound city hotels and, in the process, demonstrates that the two extremes have much in common. The InterContinental Quanzhou is closer to the latter category, standing over the waterfront in the port city for which it’s named. But its setting, within the mixed-use Tahoe Plaza retail and entertainment development, lends it something of a resort aspect; there’s even an amusement park on site.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

rest: Zhong Ji Yan Shao Fan Ya
Che Qiao Tou Wen A Shui Wan (Daxi Street)
h2: Zhong Ji Yan Shao Fan Ya
Che Qiao Tou Wen A Shui Wan (Daxi Street)

ld.name: InterContinental Lijiang Ancient Town Resort in Lijiang
ld.description: Lijiang, high in the mountains of China’s Yunnan Province, is a thriving modern city, if a smallish one by Chinese standards. But it’s best known not for its novel features but for the Old Town of Lijiang, an incredibly well-preserved 13th-century district that’s been recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It’s here, amid the ancient Naxi architecture of the Old Town, that you’ll find the InterContinental Lijiang Ancient Town Resort, which is exactly what it sounds like: a substantial modern luxury resort that does its level best to blend in with its richly historical surroundings.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The PuXuan Hotel and Spa in Beijing
ld.description: When it comes to modern high-end luxury hotels, there’s no place in the world that comes even close to being on China’s level. Not only are extravagant new towers going up in the booming secondary cities, but Beijing’s hotel scene continues to scale new heights as well. A member of the same Urban Resort Concepts group that brought us the extraordinary PuLi in Shanghai, the PuXuan Hotel and Spa is a monumental addition to the capital city’s hospitality scene.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

rest: Fortune Long Beijing Bean Sauce Noodles (East Xinglong Street)
h2: Fortune Long Beijing Bean Sauce Noodles (East Xinglong Street)

pages.h1: Four Seasons Hotel Hangzhou at West Lake

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel Hangzhou at West Lake in Hangzhou
ld.description: If there’s one overriding regional trend in luxury hospitality at the moment, it’s the rise of China’s regional cities as a high-end hotel market. Simply put, as impressive as the luxury hotels of Shanghai and Hong Kong may be, the rest of the country is catching up, if not progressing to another level entirely. Take, as an example, the Four Seasons Hotel Hangzhou at West Lake.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: Sofitel Legend Peoples Grand Hotel Xi'an

ld.name: Sofitel Legend Peoples Grand Hotel Xi'an in Xi'an
ld.description: The starting point of the Silk Road, Xi’an is one of the oldest cities in China — which, of course, is really saying something. But until fairly recent developments brought an influx of industry and business to the city, the imperial capital didn’t see many international visitors. Now with the Economist naming Xi’an one of China’s thirteen emerging megalopolises, the game’s officially on. It’s no wonder the French-owned luxury hotel chain Sofitel has opened multiple locations here, most recently the Sofitel Legend Peoples Grand Hotel Xi’an.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Park Hyatt Sanya Sunny Bay Resort

address.streetAddress: 5 Sunny Bay Road, Yalong Bay National Resort District

ld.name: Park Hyatt Sanya Sunny Bay Resort in Sanya
ld.description: They call Hainan Island the Hawaii of China, but as of this moment it may have surpassed Hawaii in at least one important respect: Hawaii suffers from an abject shortage of Park Hyatts. It’s located in a spanking-new resort community along the scenic inlet of Sunny Bay, only a couple of miles over from the longer-established Yalong Bay. So it’s safe to say you’ll have all the conveniences of home, and then some — though, Park Hyatts being what they are, you’ll be able to make it as private an experience as you like.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: No. 6 Zhujiang Road East, Tianhe District

ld.name: Rosewood Guangzhou in Tian He
ld.description: The Rosewood Guangzhou may be the tallest five-star hotel in the world, reaching all the way to the 108th floor of the CTF Finance Center. But it also scales heights that are more metaphorical, and those are the ones we’re more interested in: you’d be hard pressed to find contemporary interiors more elegant than Rosewood’s, and the views are naturally extraordinary; meanwhile the services are comprehensive, including an expansive spa, pool, and fitness center, a surplus of meeting and events space, and no fewer than seven restaurants and bars, including Too High, the vertiginous 107th-floor cocktail bar.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Peninsula Beijing in Beijing
ld.description: The Peninsula Beijing is more or less exactly what one expects from a Peninsula hotel in the Far East. This should not be taken to mean that a stay is a predictable experience, in the way that the average chain hotel experience is canned and uninspiring; rather that a visitor here may rightly expect to encounter the extremely high standard of service for which the Peninsula hotels have become known. A foolish consistency may be, as Emerson said, the hobgoblin of little minds; but the brand of consistency practiced by the Peninsula is anything but foolish.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Mandarin Oriental Shanghai in Shanghai
ld.description: Somehow it took fifty years for Mandarin Oriental to arrive in Shanghai. Given that they started out in Hong Kong, and that in the interim they managed to expand across several continents, run at least one contender for Best Hotel on Earth (that would be the Bangkok outpost), and win themselves a savvy clientele whose loyalty is the envy of the hospitality world, you’d think they might have made it here a little sooner. But no matter, for the Mandarin Oriental Shanghai already feels like a classic — the lobby perfectly dazzling, the rooms impeccably tasteful, the service fully on point from the moment they opened the doors. If even one of the 4,000 works of contemporary art was hung a hair off-kilter, we certainly haven’t found it.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Hong Po Village,  Jian Tang Town

ld.name: Banyan Tree Ringha in Shangrila
ld.description: Ten thousand feet up in the mountains of China’s southwestern Yunnan province, Banyan Tree Ringha is a bit of a departure for the Singapore-based hotel company. Though the coastal outposts of the franchise share a Balinese style, the Ringha version leaves that behind in favor of a Tibetan lodge style — this corner of Yunnan is largely Tibetan, ethnically and culturally.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Shanghai EDITION in Shanghai
ld.description: The Edition hotels combine the expertise of Ian Schrager, the original boutique hotelier, and hospitality giant Marriott International. The Edition Shanghai also draws in Ritz-Carlton, for an added measure of extravagant luxury, and the ultra-stylish local design team Neri & Hu. The rooms are chic and state-of-the-art, many with views of the Bund, and the public spaces, in classic Schrager style, are given top billing: there are five bars, including two on the rooftop, as well as a full-scale nightclub, and the restaurants include Japanese and Cantonese options as well as a modern British restaurant by chef Jason Atherton.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

rest: Lin Family of One - The Bund
h2: Lin Family of One - The Bund

pages.h1: Waldorf Astoria Shanghai on the Bund

address.streetAddress: No.2 Zhongshan Dong Yi Road, Huang Pu District

ld.name: Waldorf Astoria Shanghai on the Bund in Shanghai
ld.description: It seems they do still make 'em like they used to. The Waldorf Astoria Shanghai was a contender for the city’s best hotel from the moment it opened its doors, for there was a lot behind those doors: a soaring main hall awash in white marble, a staff that’s the epitome of discreet and attentive service, a set of restaurants that have quickly come to be regarded as top Shanghai dining destinations, and 260 elegant, oversize rooms that pull off the seemingly impossible feat of combining old-world opulence with a light, modern touch. And where better than the Bund, with its endless parade of historic architecture, for a hotel that’s something of a throwback to a past golden age of hospitality.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Sukhothai Shanghai in Shanghai
ld.description: The Sukhothai Shanghai is the long-awaited sequel to the iconic hotel of the same name in Bangkok, and it’s possessed of a grandeur that’s well suited to the occasion. While it’s more urban in setting than its Thai inspiration, it’s been imbued by virtuoso designers Neri and Hu with a tranquil, nature-reflecting atmosphere, and however ultra-modern it may be, it retains an impressive organic warmth. As for facilities and comforts, it’s in the top tier; there’s a lavish and dramatic Thai-style spa with products by Thermae, and even La Scala, the Italian restaurant, makes the trip from Bangkok to Shanghai.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

rest: Ding Te Le Zhou Mian Guan
h2: Ding Te Le Zhou Mian Guan

ld.name: Bvlgari Hotel Shanghai in Shanghai
ld.description: Like its sisters in Milan, London, and Beijing, the Bulgari Hotel Shanghai scales near-unimaginable heights of luxury while remaining always impeccably tasteful — the work, once again, of the Italian architects Antonio Citterio and Patricia Viel. The rooms occupy the top floors of a purpose-built skyscraper, atop which you’ll find the Bulgari Bar and the flagship Il Ristorante Niko Romito; the well-preserved 1916-vintage Chamber of Commerce building next door contains the Whisky Bar, the ballroom, and Bao Li Xuan, the hotel’s Cantonese restaurant. The spa, as usual, is a stunner, as are the rooms and suites.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

rest: Lin Family of One - The Bund
h2: Lin Family of One - The Bund

address.streetAddress: Parkview Green, No. 9, Dongdaqiao Road, Chaoyang

ld.name: Hotel Éclat Beijing in Beijing
ld.description: Look past Éclat Beijing’s futuristic glass-pyramid casing, and the hotel inside turns out to be one of the most high-functioning, high-pleasure business hotels in the city. And that’s saying something in a city whose hotels are undergoing something of an arms race for the business traveler, each filling its rooms with sharper and bigger screens, cushier beds and broader desks and bigger, swankier bathrooms.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Building 2, Courtyard No 8, Xinyuan South Road

ld.name: Bvlgari Hotel Beijing in Chaoyang
ld.description: In the two decades since the original Bulgari hotel opened in Milan, the brand has expanded slowly and remained true to its inspiration; the same designers, Antonio Citterio and Patricia Viel, were responsible for the Bulgari Hotel Beijing, set in the city’s relatively verdant embassy district. It’s typically luxe, with everything from butler service to Maserati car service, and the rooms and suites are tastefully extravagant. Among other highlights are the Michelin-starred Il Ristorante - Niko Romito, featuring contemporary Italian cuisine, as well as the elegant Bulgari Bar and the stylish Lounge; the hotel’s spa, with its subterranean mosaic-tile pool, is every bit the equal of its Milanese counterpart.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Park Hyatt Shenzhen in Shenzhen
ld.description: We’ve heard that Shenzhen is the capital of the future, and based on the quality of the city’s Park Hyatt, we’re inclined to believe it. It’s a tower-topping luxury hotel designed by Yabu Pushelberg, whose rooms and suites are as lavish as any in the game, and have extraordinary views of central Shenzhen through floor-to-ceiling windows. As in any Park Hyatt you can assume you’ll find a well-equipped spa, a well-lit indoor pool, and a generous handful of restaurants and bars, including the Attic, a speakeasy-style bar at the apex of this pointed 48-story tower.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

rest: Tai Shan Lao Huang Shan Fan
h2: Tai Shan Lao Huang Shan Fan

ld.name: Mandarin Oriental Wangfujing in Beijing
ld.description: Conveniently located in the city’s main shopping area, the hotel boasts generous rooms that epitomise understated elegance punctuated by subtle Chinese overtones. Some afford views of the Forbidden City, which make the experience quite unique. After a day of serious shopping, wind down at the trendy MO bar or pamper your heart and soul at the intimate spa.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: 5 Zhujiang West Road, Zhujiang New Town

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel Guangzhou in Guangzhou
ld.description: The Chinese city of Guangzhou finds the world’s luxury-hotel brands in top form, and the Four Seasons Hotel Guangzhou is a fine example. Occupying the top 30 floors of the 103-story Guangzhou International Finance Centre, it towers over the Pearl River and takes in commanding views of the entire cityscape. Eminently palatable interiors and faultless high-end comforts are the core of the Four Seasons brand, and they’re certainly present here. The spa, pool, and fitness center are impressive, as are the numerous bars and restaurants, including Catch, on the 100th floor, the city’s highest restaurant — but the most impressive space might be the vertiginous central atrium.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Qunming Lake West Street, No. 68 Shijingshan Road

ld.name: Shangri-La Shougang Park, Beijing in Beijing
ld.description: A rehabilitated industrial site on the west side of the city is now the upscale, mixed-use New Shougang High-End Industry Comprehensive Service Area; Shougang Park for short, it’s a big deal, and is home to a rather spectacular Shangri-La hotel. Designed by the Milan-based practice Lissoni & Partners, it’s meant to make a statement, and it does — it’s rare, in China or anywhere else, to find a full-featured luxury hotel that’s quite so architecturally distinguished. There’s an impressive spa and a kids’ club that’s equally full-featured, complete with a climbing wall.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: No. 4 Haitang South Road, Haitang District

ld.name: 1 Hotel Haitang Bay in Sanya
ld.description: The same 1 Hotels brand that’s responsible for green luxury-boutique hotels in Manhattan, Brooklyn, and Miami has also set up shop on the island of Hainan, one of China’s favorite leisure destinations. 1 Hotel Haitang Bay, Sanya looks particularly at home here, its unfinished eco-friendly materials echoing the island landscapes outside. Rooms are luxurious and contemporary in style, and there’s a substantial focus on wellness, from the Bamford Wellness Spa to the well-equipped Field House gym. Five pools and six restaurants and bars round out the offering; this is a fully self-sufficient luxury resort experience.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: UpperHills Block A, No. 5001 Huanggang Road, Futian District, Guangdong

ld.name: Mandarin Oriental Shenzhen in Shenzhen
ld.description: Knowing the parties involved, you might expect a Mandarin Oriental hotel in Shenzhen, China to be almost preposterously luxurious, and if that’s your instinct, you won’t be led astray. It occupies, as these things so often do, the highest floors of a 79-story skyscraper, this one right in the heart of the Futian business district. The style is stately as ever — handsome and contemporary, but equally palatable to design fans and business-hotel traditionalists. The rooms are ultra-luxe, though tastefully so, as is the 68th-floor spa; the hotel’s eight restaurants and bars include the much-in-demand Bay by Chef Fei.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

rest: Mai Yu Lao Sha Guo Zhou
Gao San Jie Dou Hua Dian
h2: Mai Yu Lao Sha Guo Zhou
Gao San Jie Dou Hua Dian

ld.name: Waldorf Astoria Beijing  in Beijing
ld.description: If you’re a real luxury-hotel freak, then simply the name Waldorf Astoria Beijing probably conveys just about all you need to know. While a cursory glance at the building’s exterior reveals that this, at least in terms of visual design, is not your grandfather’s Waldorf Astoria, the experience that’s on offer would likely be familiar to your dear old hypothetical granddad — design that’s elegant and eminently palatable, comforts that are beyond first-class, and service to rival any luxury hotel anywhere.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Andaz Shenzhen Bay in Shenzhen
ld.description: Andaz Shenzhen Bay finds itself in a particularly lively corner of China’s coastal megalopolis, surrounded by brand-new office towers and high-tech headquarters galore. Designer Tony Chi brings a bit of New York style to this outpost of Hyatt’s upscale luxury-boutique brand; the rooms are clean-lined and contemporary, but warmed by old-world touches like leather chairs and marble baths. The views of the city and the bay are impressive, as are the hotel’s facilities — from its 19-meter indoor pool to its twin restaurants, East Room and West Room, named not only for their spatial orientation but for their culinary inspirations as well.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Rissai Valley, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve in Jiuzhaigou
ld.description: Comprised of 87 villas discreetly tucked amidst the rolling hills of Jiuzhaigu, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, this serene hideaway reimagines traditional dwellings, infusing them with whispers of luxury alongside nods to Tibetan art and design. The location influences everything from the décor in the hushed accommodations, where sweeping views of the Minshan mountains invite reflection, to the spa, where treatments incorporate ancient wisdom. Three restaurants feature a blend of Sichuan, classic Chinese, and Mediterranean cuisines using local ingredients.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

address.streetAddress: Tower 2, Changsha IFS, 188 Jiefang West Road

ld.name: Park Hyatt Changsha in Changsha
ld.description: There are times when it’s perfectly fine to have your head in the clouds — and it’s when you’re staying at the Park Hyatt Changsha. This exquisite hotel occupies the top floors of the Changsha IFS Tower 2, and as the tallest building in the city (and among the tallest in the world), the views are unmatched. It’s not just what’s outside those impresses, though; the sleek sensibility perfectly marries classic Asian design with contemporary styling. With a stunning pool, fitness center, and restaurant, there’s plenty to do here, or take a ride in the elevator to visit the mall and sculpture garden.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Mandarin Oriental Qianmen in Dongcheng
ld.description: Whereas the first Mandarin Oriental hotel in Beijing occupies an ultra-modern mixed-use complex in the very center of the city, Mandarin Oriental Qianmen goes in an entirely different direction. Here you’ll find a collection of 42 hutong-style courtyard houses, in keeping with the historic Qianmen style; inside are suites that are both memorably atmospheric and state-of-the-art in their comforts — a modern luxury-hotel experience in an atmosphere of historically minded tranquility.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

rest: Fortune Long Beijing Bean Sauce Noodles (East Xinglong Street)
Chen Ji Lu Zhu Xiao Chang
h2: Fortune Long Beijing Bean Sauce Noodles (East Xinglong Street)
Chen Ji Lu Zhu Xiao Chang

address.streetAddress: No. 10, Zone 6, No. 288, Tam Wang Road

ld.name: Xitan Hotel Beijing in Beijing
ld.description: China has long been home to some of the most impressive conventional luxury hotels in the world — but it’s also home to some unusual ones, like the village-style Xitan Hotel Beijing. Despite its name, it’s located not in the city proper but in the mountains to the west, a spectacular setting for a hotel that aims to restore its guests to a closer relationship with nature.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Banyan Tree Chongqing Beibei in Chongqing
ld.description: There’s no doubt this is the Chinese Century for luxury-hotel enthusiasts; Banyan Tree, for example, counts among its offerings nearly as many properties in China as in the rest of the world combined. Banyan Tree Chongqing Beibei stakes its territory in the mountainous northern outskirts of the city of Chongqing, and in so doing exposes a global audience to the region’s rugged beauty — and its natural hot springs.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: T7, No.1 Shenzhen Bay, No. 3008, Zhongxin Road, Nanshan District

ld.name: Raffles Shenzhen in Shenzhen
ld.description: Raffles has come a long way since its 19th-century beginning in colonial Singapore; here the brand occupies the prominent central tower of the ultra-modern mixed-use One Shenzhen Bay complex. Raffles Shenzhen, however, is neither entirely historical nor entirely futuristic, but blends elements of both worlds; rooms and suites contain classic elements, for example, even as they look out over Shenzhen Bay from an astonishing height.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Waldorf Astoria Shanghai Qiantan in Pudong
ld.description: For some time now the luxury hotels of China have felt like dispatches from the future of hospitality. And while Waldorf Astoria Shanghai Quintan’s name might suggest a hint of turn-of-the-20th-century New York, today’s Waldorf Astoria brand is not about nostalgia. Waldorf Astoria Shanghai Qiantan occupies an eye-catching contemporary building on the banks of the Huangpu River, and inside it blends a dizzying array of aesthetic influences, from Art Deco to modernism and beyond.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Yanbai Villa, Beijing in Beijing
ld.description: A 12th-century painting provided the initial inspiration for Yanbai Villa, and it’s clear from the results that the Pritzker Prize–winning architect Wang Shu has delivered a fitting tribute. It’s a stunning piece of architecture, and an impressive hotel as well, standing on the wooded shores of Yanqi Lake, on the northeastern fringes of Beijing.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: The St. Regis on the Bund, Shanghai

address.streetAddress: Dong 2nd East Road, 538 Zhong Shan Lu, Huang Pu Qu

ld.name: The St. Regis on the Bund, Shanghai in Huangpu
ld.description: The Shanghai Bund is the city’s famed riverfront district, notable for (among other things) its wealth of examples of historical architectural styles — the one place, arguably, that an exact replica of the original St. Regis New York might make sense. But the St. Regis on the Bund, Shanghai is no period reconstruction. This is classic St. Regis opulence adapted to its environment, a 21st-century luxury hotel that seamlessly combines modern and traditional influences. Many of the rooms and suites take in impressive views of the river and the Bund skyline, and all are memorably styled and state-of-the-art in comfort. Make time for the hotel’s legendary afternoon tea service.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: J Hotel, Shanghai Tower in Pudong
ld.description: Shanghai Tower is not just any tower, but the tallest building in China, of which J Hotel Shanghai Tower occupies floors 84 to 105 (plus a restaurant on the 120th, of which more later), giving it a view over this magnificent city that no competitor can match. Nor is height the only thing J Hotel has going for it — this is in every respect a luxury experience, marked by an opulence that’s only appropriate given its elevated position.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The St. Regis Shenzhen Bao'an in Shenzhen
ld.description: Shenzhen's Bao'an District occupies the western edge of the Pearl River Delta, looking out over Qianhai Bay toward Hong Kong. The St. Regis arrived here in February 2025, bringing its second address in the city: 289 rooms across 51 floors where dark oak parquet, Carrara marble bathrooms and intricate marquetry woodwork give the interiors a weight and craftsmanship that the building's glass exterior doesn't hint at. Emerald-hued sofas and sweeping bay views define the living areas. Yan Ting does seasonal Cantonese; the Drawing Room on the 35th floor, framed around Caroline Astor lore, serves afternoon tea, and the rooftop terrace bar is where the city comes into focus.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: No. 1, Wu Nangding, Jushui Village, Shengping Town

ld.name: Deqin Meri Poodom in Deqin
ld.description: At 3,600 meters on a Meili Snow Mountain viewing platform, this hotel by designer Wu Bin approaches architecture as spiritual theater. The structure plays with angular stone walls and sharp lines that mirror the Himalayan ridges behind it, interiors stripping back to essentials: textured stone corridors, meditative courtyards, handcrafted furniture in pale wood. Rooms are built around the view, large windows turning every sunrise over the peaks into the main event. Public spaces emphasize scale and light, sculptural staircases and walls of glass that dissolve the line between lobby and landscape. More sculpture than hotel, it belongs to the elevation as much as the town below.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: No. 5016 Shennan Road East, Luohu District

ld.name: The St. Regis Shenzhen in Shenzhen
ld.description: Where better than 100 stories above China’s unofficial high-tech capital for the St. Regis brand to find a harmonious blend of its storied past and its optimistic future? The St. Regis Shenzhen stands atop the Kingkey 100 skyscraper, from which its 290 rooms and suites take in extraordinarily far-ranging views. The interiors admit of a wealth of stylistic influences, from Art Deco to street art, and the resulting atmosphere is both glamorous and memorable. Butler service is among the benefits, and the six restaurants and bars are supplemented by the city’s many ground-level offerings.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Sanya EDITION in Sanya
ld.description: On Hainan Island’s southern coast, The Sanya Edition turns fifty acres of waterfront into a contemporary sanctuary. At its center lies a vast man-made “private ocean,” a feature that anchors the resort’s play between water, light, and landscape: bamboo groves, lotus pools, and lanterns that drift across the surface at night. Every room faces the sea, while restaurants float, spill onto the sand, or rise above the palms. Sleek yet deeply atmospheric, it reimagines tropical luxury through a distinctly Chinese lens.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Yihe Mansions in Nanjing
ld.description: Step down from Yihe Road into a collection of Republican-era villas where China's political elite once lived beneath the maples. The architecture remains intact: courtyards, carved details, generous rooms bathed in filtered light. Inside, lacquered wood meets understated furniture, antique ceramics sit alongside contemporary art. Each villa functions independently and the Mansions have their own restaurant, spa, and small museum. The surrounding gardens blur the line between indoors and out. It's not a hotel recreating history, but history adapted for modern comfort, thoughtfully and without ostentation.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Amanfayun in Hangzhou
ld.description: Privacy, discretion, understatement, and above all absolute tastefulness in every conceivable detail: this is the stuff an Aman hotel is made of. At Amanfayun, the brand’s Hangzhou outpost, set amidst the tea fields and bamboo groves on the outskirts of town, those values translate into 46 luxurious courtyard dwellings, each one an authentic traditional Chinese courtyard home, meticulously restored and retrofitted to a luxurious modern standard.
